title: Culturing Euplotes crassus to High Densities Using Algae and Bacteria
author: Lawrence A. Klobutcher
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2aggabw
materials: Gently invert tubes daily to disperse settled material.

steps.title: Grow E. coli overnight
steps.instruction: Inoculate 10 ml of L‑broth with E. coli (strain HT115 or any strain) and incubate overnight without antibiotics.

steps.title: Distribute and pellet bacteria
steps.instruction: Aliquot the overnight E. coli culture into 2 ml microcentrifuge tubes and centrifuge in a microcentrifuge for 1.5 min to pellet the cells.

substeps.instruction: Distribute the bacterial culture to 2 ml microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in algae culture
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and resuspend each bacterial pellet in 2 ml of a moderately dense culture of Dunaliella salina grown in artificial seawater.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 2 ml of the Dunaliella salina culture.

steps.title: Combine Euplotes with algae and bacteria
steps.instruction: In a 15 ml disposable plastic tube, mix 1 ml lightly starved Euplotes crassus culture, 7 ml moderately dense Dunaliella salina culture (artificial seawater), and 2 ml of the resuspended E. coli culture.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml lightly starved Euplotes crassus culture.
Add 7 ml moderately dense Dunaliella salina culture grown on artificial seawater.
Add 2 ml resuspended E. coli culture.

steps.title: Incubate cultures at room temperature
steps.instruction: Place the tubes at an angle and incubate at room temperature for about 5 days; Euplotes should consume the bacteria and algae and reach ~3,000 cells ml⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for ~5 days.
